While the story has a consistent tone and setting, it lacks an underlying narrative unity and a logical progression of events that propel a plot forward. It consists largely of mundane, disconnected observations and routine interactions (collecting fare, directing cars, noticing a loose seal on the door, thinking about a shopping list) that do not build toward anything. The ending introduces an entirely new element—a phone call from an unintroduced character named "Jonas" that Ilse ignores—which has no connection to the preceding scenes with the passengers, leaving the story feeling disjointed and unresolved rather than a harmonious, satisfying whole.
